title: Sharbel Makhlouf (24 July)
hook: a Maronite hermit of Lebanon, who kept silence for years

segments.voice: Yesterday, Camillus de Lellis, the gambler who became a nurse to the sick. Your line was the red cross. Which nurse did you thank? Day one thousand ten.

High in the mountains of Lebanon, above a monastery, there is a small stone hermitage. One monk lives there. He rises in the dark to pray. He works the vineyard with his hands. He eats once a day, tradition says, and very little. He speaks only when he must. Visitors who climb up to see him find a man who mostly says nothing at all. He wrote no books that we know of. He gave no famous sermons. And yet today pilgrims crowd the road to that mountain. Today, a saint whose teaching was silence.
screen: `A HERMITAGE IN THE MOUNTAINS.` → `PRAYER, VINES, ONE MEAL.` → `A MAN WHO SAYS NOTHING.`

segments.voice: Sharbel Makhlouf was a monk of the Maronite Church. The Maronites are Eastern Catholics, rooted in Lebanon, in full communion with the pope, with their own ancient liturgy, prayed in part in Syriac, a form of Aramaic, close to the language Jesus spoke. So this is a Catholic saint, and also a saint from a different branch of the Catholic family than some listeners know. He was born with another name and took the name Sharbel when he became a monk. After years in the monastery, he asked to live as a hermit, and he spent the rest of his life in that hermitage, in prayer and silence, for many years, tradition says. Why silence? In the books of Kings, Elijah waits on a mountain for God. A great wind passes, then an earthquake, then fire, and the Lord is not in them. Then, in the Douay-Rheims: "after the fire a whistling of a gentle air." Not in the noise. In the quiet after it. Stories gathered around him even while he lived. Tradition tells of a lamp the other monks filled with water as a test, and it burned anyway. After his death, the stories multiplied, of light seen at his grave, of healings, and pilgrims began to come and still do. The Church examined these claims before naming him a saint. But the heart of it is simple. A man went quiet for God, for years, and that quiet still draws people up a mountain.
screen: `A MONK OF THE MARONITE CHURCH.` · `HE ASKED TO LIVE AS A HERMIT.` · `GOD IN THE QUIET AFTER THE FIRE.` · `QUIET THAT STILL DRAWS PEOPLE.` · then, large: `A WHISTLING OF A GENTLE AIR.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: keep silence, on purpose. Settle, and breathe. For these two minutes, no words, not even in your head if you can help it. When a sentence starts, let it trail off. Hear what's left: the room, the street, your breath. If you pray, you can rest in that gentle air from Elijah's mountain, and let the rest go. If you don't, simply let the quiet be enough. And if you can, after the bell, keep going, and make it five minutes. The bell holds the time.
Sharbel Makhlouf. A Maronite monk of Lebanon who lived his last years as a hermit, in prayer and silence.
Your line: silence of lebanon. Today, find five minutes with no screen, no music, no talk, and keep them. Day one thousand ten.
